```suggestion
			[b]Note:[/b] When this option is active, [signal AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback.state_finished] will never be emitted for the last node.
```

This condition looks a odd. It might work in the looping case described in the description, but wouldn’t the transition stop in cases where there is no loop? For example:

Your case:
```
A <=> B✏️
```

No loop case (maybe A can't transition to C if B is Ended):
```
A -> B✏️ -> C
```

So the correct approach would be to skip the nested ended state (without processing 1 frame) rather than stopping the transition to stay in the current state.

Thank for your the review! I am not sure I understand your concerns, so let me try to clarify my understanding, and you can ask for more details if needed.

What this change will do is that for the case where we would normally transition to End specifically, it will instead stay at the current node, but instruct the parent that a transition should be made by making sure that `get_remain()` will return 0. It is true that the inner state machine will no longer progress after this point, but the parent will. This is true regardless of whether the animation inside the state machine is looping or not.

But maybe you are not talking about a looped animation here, I don't quite understand what A, B and C are representing in your example.

Additionally, if the inner state machine is of root type, it will be reset when entering the next time. If it's nested, execution will be resumed on the node right before end, which is a change in behavior and one of the reasons why I decided to put it behind a new property.

I see you edited your comment and added the pens, that helps a lot, thanks! That scenario works just fine even with this change. See the attached images and let me know if I have understood your concern correctly.

Can you upload the MRP where the issue clearly occurs? It’s possible that the Description setup is incorrect to begin with. If you're talking about a case involving an xfade, I believe this PR is equivalent to using a "Nested" state and "not connecting" it to the end. Also as I recall, the author of https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/98617 intended to crossfade between A and C without going through B in the `A -> B✏️ -> C` case, and I don't think this PR addresses that issue. Instead, we should probably handle it the way https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/112709. Even though the work is still in progress, it’s fine to salvage it if you want.

Sure! Just open this project and make sure the animation tree is playing (barbarian should be running). Then try toggling "Condition" on and off to observe the problem. You will see how, when transitioning out of the inner state machine, the character goes into a t-pose before crossfading with the target animation. If you have my branch, you can then try enabling "Defer End" for the inner state machine and observe the issue going away. Please let me know if you need anything else :slightly_smiling_face: [MRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28574211/MRP.zip)

After looking at the MRP, I understood the problem. So I determine that what is clearly missing here is "BreakLoopAtEnd" in the "Nested" mode StateMachine. In Nested mode, the system will treat a path as a dead end and terminate the animation even if it isn't connected to the "End" node. However, there is no way to exit a loop animation.

It's very important that a looped animation in an inner state machine can be exited based on a condition, so that it's possible to create systems such as mine and the one described in #98617. If you read the discussion in the mentioned issue, all of the other suggestions (including #112709). are missing the point that both me and the OP of #98617 want to be able to set up complex state machines with conditional states without having to write scripts for it. 

That #112709 would be the preferred solution is based on a conclusion by the other people participating in that issue, and does not reflect the intention of the OP, is at least my interpretation of it.

This PR solves the problem by adding a way to prevent blending with the End node of an inner state machine, and therefore works around it, allowing us to use inner state machines the way that I assume people expect them to work. I don't think anyone actually expects to blend with the t-pose (RESET animation) in this case.

What do you suggest would be the next course of action?

I've modified the MRP to use Nested. I thought I couldn't get out of Nested, but it was my misunderstanding (since that MRP was not using break loop option) and it was able to get out.

If that works, I think this PR's changes is not necessary. Then, I think you just close this PR, and it would be helpful to add something like a tutorial to the documentation repository (https://github.com/godotengine/godot-docs) if you want to clarify this case.

[MRP-fixed.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28574876/MRP-fixed.zip)

This solves the problem, but only for the MRP. The more complex cases will still be problematic. The problem for the "real" case is that you cannot put the condition for the exit transition in the outer state machine, because different paths inside the inner state machine can have different conditions. I have attached an updated MRP which showcases such an advanced scenario. [Advanced-MRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28575065/Advanced-MRP.zip) In my real game, I have an even more advanced setup, where I can move to the inner state machine from two outer states (Idle and Walking). This is the reason why the inner state machine is even needed.

Based on that MRP, I think what is missing is the functionality to reset to Start for the "Nested" type. I have reproduced that in the script below, and it should work.

[Advanced-fixed.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28575327/Advanced-fixed.zip)

However, resetting to Start will make it indistinguishable from the Root type. If you want to control that, perhaps one way would be to provide a `Custom` enum separate from `Root`/`Nested`/`Grouped`, and allow individual settings such as "whether to return to Start when a reset occurs" and "whether to treat a dead end as an End."

In any case, I do not think the current implementation of this PR is in the right direction. Therefore, the suggested approach would be to close this PR and create a new one to add the `Custom` mode to Enum.

If there are many cases where you need to control these, perhaps you should eventually leave only `Grouped` and `Custom` (so finally it become `bool is_grouped`) in 5.0, and interpret Root and Nested as presets for Custom.

Also, for the Nested type, I believe that states with significantly different exit conditions should not be placed in the same StateMachine in the first place. In the Nested type, the transition conditions to dead-end states are more important than the exit conditions.

Alternatively, another approach would be to allow multiple ports for "Grouped" mode StateMachines, which would be one of the right path. The Grouped mode reproduces the behavior of transitioning directly to the parent StateMachine without blending rest pose. See also https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/88878.

@TokageItLab I was somewhat invested in this PR due to my issue #115382 requiring a similar solution, an "At End" exit out of a inner Root statemachine without hitting the T-pose.

I want to ask: what is the purpose of ever encountering a T pose apart from the outermost State Machine? To put it another way: why ever treat any inner End state as a T pose rather than an anticipated transition out of the StateMachine? I have many complex cases in my game that keep seeing the T pose get mixed into transition frames, where a freeze at the last animation before end would be far preferable. As a result, I end up having to avoid inner StateMachines most of the time, and design more complicated trees.

Is this really not a bug? What behaviour would not having a RESET there break? If this is indeed intended, then surely the amount of times it is erroneously encountered (even though a transition has been adequately provided) has to be a bug, at least?

Would appreciate your thoughts, here or in my issue. The gameplay demo in that issue shows the real-world problem it causes, and there are many more instances that I've had to work around.

I haven't been intentionally playing the End state as a T-pose. Essentially, the internal blend amount of the StateMachine is 0 on the Start/End state, which means the Rest/RESET animation is simply being applied as a fallback.

And I don't think there is any issue with Start and End being treated as a RESET animation due to this fallback. In a deterministic AnimationTree, there is likely no other way to handle cases where the system remains at Start or End without prev/next transitions. Especially for Root/Nested are not designed to allow child StateMachines to view the state of their parent StateMachine.

Also, there is an option called reset_ends for intentionally playing the End state as a RESET animation. When this is set to false and if there is xfade, the xfade time is considered for the transition to the End state, but blending with the RESET animation does not occur. (However, if it transitions to End immediately after the xfade finishes and remains there, it will result in a RESET animation = T-pose).

Upon re-examining the Final MRP above (in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/119748#discussion_r3352802282), I found that the xfade time of the internal StateMachine's transition to the End was 0. Matching it with the xfade time of the parent StateMachine was all that was actually needed to solve the problem.

[Final-fixed-by-xfade.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29137233/Final-fixed-by-xfade.zip)

If the T-pose is still being played after matching the xfade times between the parent and the internal state machine, it implies that a bug is occurring somewhere that is processing unintended frames after ending xfade or unintended interrupt the crossfade. In other words, the main cause of the T-pose appearing should be a discrepancy somewhere regarding the intended timing of the End state.

While not transitioning to the End state and instead holding the last frame of the previous state is one possible workaround, it only corrects the "pose drawn during an unintended frame" and is not the correct path to prevent the "drawing of an unintended frame" itself.

This leaves the animation momentarily stranded inside the inner statemachine, resulting in a T pose on exit.

Any `Root` inner StateMachine of moderate complexity may have variable xfade paths both to the end and out from the StateMachine - which is entirely resonable and is needed to make games. It is not feasible to account for the xfade from every state to end and out from the StateMachine to other states to be the exact same, so encountering the undesirable T pose becomes inevitable.

As for why `Nested` isn't suitable to use, apart from the reset to Start that's needed, it cannot reliable escape when `At End` is expected on the outside, [as I explain here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/115382#issuecomment-3800792328).

Regardless of what the the logic is,
1. I cannot foresee any instance where a developer would intentionally desire the T pose's appearance (for a frame or two) on the way out of a StateMachine, I can't see why making this change should be viewed as altering intended behaviour rather than making a long-needed change.
2. The fact that the developer themselves might not encounter this but the player might in-game, through no fault of either of them, just makes the engine appear more error-prone.
3. Similar to how solving #95688 was needed to complete root motion implementation, I truly believe this is needed as a step to complete the StateMachine implementation. It simply isn't reliable as anything other than the root of the AnimationTree otherwise.

For the points above, I request that the animation team reconsiders this, and can approve a PR that can guard against this quirk of StateMachine proactively, either with this PR if it can also solve #115382, or [@spinalcord's](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/115382#issuecomment-4400490037), whichever would be a more suitable solution.

Alternatively, would it be appropriate to the case implemented here as an added part when `reset_ends` is false, since it already implies avoiding the RESET pose?

As I have said many times, if you want to keep it stopped at a specific frame, you can use Nested mode. Also, ending at an arbitrary timing is possible with a transition to the End with xfade when reset_ends = false. If an unintended End state execution occurs there, the problem lies outside the End state behavior. I believe this judgment remains unchanged.

The most issue where the animation of the previous state is retained when transitioning from Root/Nested to End, as seen in this PR and the commit you mentioned, is that it becomes completely unclear what the actual state is when the `current_state` the user has retrieved is "End".

And not only that, but Nested mode will not go to Start when reset unless it is an End state, instead restarting the animation of the current state from the beginning. This raises questions about how to handle this "fake end" scenario, requiring us to rethink the definition of "End" in multiple places, which could reduce maintainability.

It simply isn't reliable as anything other than the root of the AnimationTree otherwise.

Regarding the case you mentioned where you want to have multiple xfade values for End in an inner StateMachine, I think the correct approach is to improve Grouped mode to have multiple Ends and expose multiple ports (although we might be able to apply multipe port/ends to Root/Nested mode as well). That means, if you absolutely want to disallow fallbacks at Start/End, improving the usability of Grouped mode, which interprets Start/End conceptually rather than as actual States, should be the most logical approach.

No. I’ve said this many times before, but what this PR is attempting to implement which holds the previous state without transitioning to "End" should not be implemented, even in Custom mode. As I sent in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/119748#discussion_r3442552794, the only thing missing in your case was the correct setting for xfade in the transition to the End in your MRP.

As explained above, Custom mode simply exposes the branching logic that depends on the two existing Root/Nested options: "detect_dead_end: whether to treat dead ends as the end of the StateMachine" and "keep_state_on_reset: whether to transition to Start when reset (internal seek to 0) occurs while in a state other than the End state".

In other words, since only 2 of the 4 possible combinations are currently available, like:

- `Root`: detect_dead_end = false, keep_state_on_reset = false
- `Nested`: detect_dead_end = true, keep_state_on_reset = true

`Custom` mode will expose two boolean variables to allow selection from those 4 combinations, then `Root/Nested` are become the template for those boolean options.

Anything beyond that should be handled through additional implementation, such as implementing multiple ends/ports, as also explained above.

Another possibility to consider might be implementing a helper function (on the Editor) that statically copies the parent's xfade and propagates it to the inner StateMachine to handle cases where the xfade on the transition to the End in the inner state machine is not configured as intended, like https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/119748#discussion_r3442552794 case.

None of the three recommendations I listed (Custom mode / multiple Ends / xfade helper) are tightly coupled or conflict with one another, but introducing cases where the flow does not transition to "End" as in this PR will cause issues to spread throughout the StateMachine code and will undoubtedly lead to a combination explosion, then loss of maintainability.
